newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania PM asks parliament to lift emergency.
newsitem.headline: Albania PM asks parliament to lift emergency.

text.p: Prime Minister Bashkim Fino urged Albania's parliamentary speaker on Friday to reconvene the dissolved parliament so that it could lift a state of emergency before elections set for June 29.
"It would be the honourable course for parliament, which declared the state of emergency in March, to lift it now," he told state-owned television.

"It is nonsense to hold elections under emergency conditions," added Fino, a member of the Socialist Party which has strongly advocated that the state of emergency and a 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. curfew should be lifted before the vote.
Parliamentary speaker Pjeter Arbnori, widely seen as one of President Sali Berisha's closest allies, earlier dismissed calls for him to reconvene parliament.
"We cannot lift the state of emergency before restoring constitutional order," he said. "The state of emergency is a barrier to none, only to violence."
Fino said he deeply regretted that Arbnori had refused to meet constitutional obligations allowing the prime minister to summon the parliament even when it was dissolved.
Several opposition parties have threatened to boycott the elections, viewed as a crucial element in defusing political tension in Europe's poorest nation, if the state of emergency was lifted.
